text_fidelity_a:
Logo Party Board Game I gave this game to my teenage nephew, who played it with several family members and friends. They found the instructions not really hard, but very long and involved, and it took awhile for them to figure out how to play the game. They tried to follow the rules, but ended up playing the game according to their own "house rules."

The game comes with a timer, which makes a very loud noise. They eventually stopped using the timer because the noise was so annoying. One player even thought that the timer might have been broken. The timer went off completely on its own, making that obnoxious noise. Another player, an adult woman, did not enjoy the game at all, but the teens enjoyed the aspect of the game that required you to draw or to describe a product or the logo or symbol for a product. The game seems to be a combination of Pictionary and Charades and Trivial Pursuit. The kids thought this was a good, creative game, with a combination of old and new products. This aspect of the game made it good for mixed age groups. As other reviewers have said, this game is best played in teams. I have the feeling that this experiment may have gone better if at least one player had really understood how to play the game so that so much time would not have been consumed in trying to understand the rules.

The teens are willing to give this game another try. I am going to edit this review after they do to see if they enjoyed the game more. I have a feeling they will, especially as they become more familiar with it.
text_fidelity_b: Logo Party Board Game

LEGO City Race Boat Transporter 60254 Race Boat Toy, Fun Building Set for Kids (238 Pieces) This LEGO CITY RACE BOAT TRANSPORTER BUILDING SET ((60254) New 2020, 238 Pieces) is fairly easy to build--the difficulty is what I’d call “normal” for a City-themed set. City sets are among my favorites, because they include fire trucks, police stations, buses, trains, beachgoer minifigs, space stations, and all the rest of the things that a bustling city (or the airspace above it) needs. This particular set is aimed at ages 5 and up.

The set contains all the pieces required to build three separate items: a semi-trailer truck (for towing the race boat), a trailer for hauling the race boat, and a race boat. (You can use the truck’s trailer hitch to tow other things that you build, of course.)

The “Xtreme” graphics are NOT printed on the pieces, but are applied with stickers. (I hate stickers, too.) Applying stickers is made easier if you first stick a corner to something long and thin (e.g., a spudger or a plastic knife) so that you can better control the placement on the element. A good thing about LEGO stickers is that they can be removed and replaced (like Post-Its) if you get them misaligned.

The LEGO elements are compatible with other City sets and with all regular LEGO sets (but not with DUPLO sets, which have extra-large pieces for very young builders). The Race Boat Transporter set is another fine addition to the extensive collection of City sets.
text_fidelity_b: LEGO City Race Boat Transporter 60254 Race Boat Toy, Fun Building Set for Kids (238 Pieces)

Outset Media Picture Charades – No Reading Required – Preschool Game for Ages 4 and up, Multi includes 192 Cards, Instructions. I wish I could give this more than 5 stars. My little 4 year old is always jealous of his older siblings' board games, he often pretends he can play or asks "to be on a team" so he can be part of the fun. But with this, he can actually play unassisted! The game is simple, it's charades but no reading is required. Each card is just a picture, and it is up to the player's interpretation to act out. For example, if a kid doesn't know the difference between a crossing guard and a police officer, that's fine! Whatever word they think it was, they act out and everyone else guesses! There are no wrong ways to interpret it, so any child with an imagination can play!
He loves this game so much, we even took it recently on a trip to visit his grandparents. If you have a child who is too young to play games that require reading, this is an absolute treasure. I can't believe it took this long for someone to realize the market potential for this. LOVE it!

You don't need to own anything else if you have this, because it includes two fully ready-to-play decks.

One of those decks, as advertised on the box, is Mewtwo. The other is not Melmetal - it is the same Pikachu deck from the Battle Academy set, including the same book from that set that will teach you about half of the rules of how to play.

It also comes with sleeves - one set for Mewtwo, and the other for Melmetal, which is strange considering that he's not in the box.

text_fidelity_a:
The Chameleon, Award-Winning Board Game for Families & Friends…… If you're familiar with the game Spyfall, then you're going to be able to jump right into this game. This one is quirkier, faster, but fortunately, has more replayability than Spyfall does.

In The Chameleon, each player is given a code card, or a card that says "You're the Chameleon." If you have a code card, you look up a word on a shared board, and if you're The Chameleon, you attempt to blend in with everyone else. After a little bit of finding and thinking time, each player says one word, even the Chameleon. Each player is then to attempt to argue and deduce who the Chameleon player is. Everyone votes, and that player is revealed. If it's not the Chameleon, then that player has done a good job of blending in and is the winner of the round. If it is the Chameleon, then that player gets the opportunity to guess the secret word that everyone else knew. If they get it right, they win. If not, everyone else wins.

Rounds of this game are fast, and that's a great thing. After repeat plays, it becomes fairly easy to identify the Chameleon player, but that's when the game really starts. Were you vague enough with your words so that they cannot figure out the secret code word?

There is enough replayability in this box to make the game fun for a wide range of groups, and a larger number of players. There are 40 different category clues, which means that there are 640 different possible words you could have, and that far exceeds the 20 locations of Spyfall.

Two issues prevent this from being a 5* game. The first is component quality. It's bad. Cards are awkwardly sized and flimsy, there are remainder marks on the edges of some cards from where they were cut. The second issue is that there simply aren't enough mapping location cards in the box. There's really only two possible sets of locations, and while there are no players who will be able to memorize the exact locations of words, it's possible that repeat mappings occur, and Chameleons with outstanding memories will be able to guess with regularity by reading the dice.
text_fidelity_b: The Chameleon, Award-Winning Board Game for Families & Friends……

Depointer Life Inflatable Tank Float with Water Cannon Squirt Water Gun Toy Pool Tank Float for Kids Adult Summer Pool Party REVIEW UPDATE JUNE 30, 2022:
---------------------------------------
* We were finally able to take this tank for a spin. It is indeed super fun. But here are 3 noteworthy things:

1.) It is gigantic, adult supervision is required to make sure kids get in and out of it safely. Never allow them to stand up to get out. Buoyancy can cause them to flip and hit the side of the pool cement. So make sure they simply crawl off the tank slowly and safely, like rolling out of bed. LOL!
2.) It takes forever to blow it up, even with an electronic inflator. So if you want to avoid anxious kids, then prepare it the day before, or at least 30 minutes before swim time.
3.) The water gun is not as I imagined. There is no trigger. It's a pump action. A clear straw/pipe dangles through the bottom into the pool, so you can constantly pump water. It is difficult for little children. So the idea that whoever is in the tank has the advantage is wrong. LOL! In our pool, we all have water guns, and whoever is in the tank becomes the target. LOL! Nevertheless, it's still very fun, and the 5-Star rating is justified.

ORIGINAL REVIEW MAY 4th, 2022:
----------------------------------------

THE GOOD:
---------------
* Seems like super fun!
* 61"x44"x24" is a very substantial size. So this is not for little above ground pools.
* The vinyl feels pretty standard. It did not feel thin or cheap.
* Everything seems to be complete. It even included little repair stickers in case you get holes.

THE BAD:
------------
* Well, we won't exactly know yet until the summer. I got this for the upcoming summer, and I'll be sure to update. My kids can't wait. For now, gotta give it 5-Stars.

Crayola Glow Book I never really thought I would be calling any toy a godsend, but the Crayola Glow Book has done something for my ten-year-old son that none of his school teachers (and certainly not his art teacher) has been able to do. I've tried, too. I've tried asking, showing, cajoling, ordering, limiting privileges, exaggerated sighing, and using his full name, but my child's penmanship is abysmal and his art skills mostly stink.

The reason for this is relatively straightforward: in my family, kids develop their fine motor skills later than most kids do. My parents and teachers made me work at it, but I at least was getting a lot of practice all the time. My child goes to a school where he gets to type a lot of his assignments. He's learned a lot in art about color and perspective and design, but he gets extremely frustrated trying to execute what's in his head, so he stopped enjoying drawing and painting pretty much as soon as he hit kindergarten.

When I ordered this, I thought it was going to turn out to be just a gimmicky gadgety thing he'd use once and then I'd get to use it to leave notes my husband would have to work to ignore, but my son loves it. He can write, draw, erase, illuminate, and animate without having to commit anything to paper or to critical eyes (except his own). Because the illustration plates are layered, if he's happy with one part but not another, he can re-do the one without having to worry about smudging or wrecking the other. As a result, he is spending time using his fine motor skills, they are improving, and he is much happier with the work he is doing.

I gave this five stars for fun, based on his recommendation. I rate it five stars for educational value and five stars overall for how much help it has been in an area in which my child needed some help. I gave it four stars for durability. It feels a little flimsy, but it's holding up well so far.

UPDATE: When you exhaust the markers that come with this, you can use dry erase markers on it. They're actually a little bit easier to see and work with, they come in tons of colors, and they clean right up.
text_fidelity_b: Crayola Glow Book

Thames & Kosmos Big Engineering Makerspace | Science Kit | 22 Physics Lessons & Experiments | Toy of The Year Award Finalist | Homeschool | Learning Pod | STEM Kit This THAMES & KOSMOS THE BIG ENGINEERING MAKERSPACE SCIENCE EXPERIMENT KIT is the real deal--a fun model-building kit that painlessly teaches basic concepts of physics (e.g., thermal air currents, levers, momentum). Each model (e.g., crane, helicopter) actually works, and is accompanied by a “what's happening here” explanation in the manual of why it works (e.g., turning a crank hoists a crane load by exerting force on a rope threaded through pulleys that share the weight to be lifted; a helicopter’s fast tail rotor produces a force that counteracts the main rotor’s force to stabilize the helicopter).

The models are assembled from plastic parts (some parts are similar to LEGO Technic elements) by following clear step-by-step diagrams (similar to LEGO building instructions). They are powered by a pressurized air tank controlled by a switch with a lever. There are no batteries to buy or charge, because you pressurize the air tank by pumping air into it (the pump assembly resembles a bicycle tire pump).

Each model has suggestions for finding out more about the scientific principles that relate to it. The manual indicates the difficulty level of each model with a three-dot system (easy, medium, difficult).

This kit may seem expensive (about $90 on Amazon), but it teaches a LOT about the practical application of physical and engineering principles, for the price of a single medium-sized LEGO Technic kit. It's a kit to use in home schooling, or to give to a child who really wants to understand why and how construction equipment, vehicles, watercraft, aircraft, and cameras work in the real world.

text_fidelity_a:
Civilization A New Dawn Board Game | Tactical Strategy Game for Adults and Teens Based on the Hit Video Game Series | Ages 14+ | 2-4 Players | Average Playtime 1-2 Hours | Made by Fantasy Flight Games Short version of the review: it’s a fun game with a pretty good first-game learning curve that settles in pretty quickly in subsequent games. It can be long (though you can adjust it). We’ll add it to our rotation of “lengthy” games

Longer version

1) Packing
I’m going to ding the game for packaging because while everything comes fine (as is typical, there’s a lot of popping pieces out of their cardboard sheets), I like when games include easy ways of keeping thing together and/or organized once you’ve played the first game. Even if it’s as minimal as separate small plastic bags. We used our own tiny bags (we’ve learned to keep ones that do come with other games if they’re extra thanks to consolidation) and a few regular small baggies, but I don’t think it’s too much to ask that those things be included

2) Materials
All the materials seem of good quality. Cards are not super-thick but they’re not at all flimsy, the non-plastic pieces feel solid and you don’t have any sense that they’ll start coming apart or getting dented/torn. The plastic cities are a nice touch, but the capital cities could perhaps have been made a little more distinctive. Not at all a big deal; a close look is all you need.

3) Instructions
The big sheet of instructions is fine. Generally clear and well written, with a few “clarification” points at the end, which is a nice touch. We had a few questions that weren’t included, but they were easy to find online. A few individual player cards with a stripped down bit of instruction for quick, easy reference would have been nice to toss in

4) Set up
As noted (and as is usual for these types of games) there’s a lot of popping things out and organizing. Once that’s done the first time, set-up is relatively quick. You put together some map tiles which is easy enough (though this 50+-year-old wouldn’t have minded if the organizing numbers were a little bigger on each tile). Each player gets tokens, a set of cards five of which are laid out in a particular order under their “Focus” bar (the cards are in these areas: Military, Technology, Culture, Economy, Industry), a set of “diplomacy” cards, a “leader” card (who they “play”—Cleopatra for instance), a few caravans (little wagons used for trading). After you’ve done it a few times it’s a pretty quick set-up. You also set up some cards to the side of the play area (World Wonder cards and City-State Diplomacy Cards and Victory Cards (these are what determine how the game is won). This is always an issue in these sorts of game because of course they’re not going to be truly “visible” to all the players. Someone is going to have to move or ask to see them to see what they say (some change throughout the game). I have no idea how to get around that though; it’s just a matter of physical setting.

5) game play
I’m not going to detail it. But generally, the Victory cards have two “agendas” on them, such as build two Wonders of the World, and a player who achieves one agenda from each of the cards is the winner (this is nice because you can shorten the game if desired by simply playing with fewer Victory cards). As far as the play itself
1) Players can “resolve” (do what it says) any one of the five cards below their Focus bar. This might mean building a city, attacking someone, moving a caravan, laying out a “Control” piece to claim a hex space (i.e. territory).
2) Once they’ve done that, that card gets move to slot one under the bar and all the others move one slot to the right. This is key because the slot number affects how the card is resolved. For instance, when you attack using your military card, you roll a die and add the slot number (and possibly other bonuses) to your roll. So you’re going to want to attack when that card is in the 4 or 5 position typically, not the 1 or 2 slot. This adds a nice bit of complexity to your action choices.

That’s pretty much the gameplay for players. A few other factor include
1) You can swap out a card under your focus by advancing your “Tech” counter a certain number (you do that using one of the cards). Once you hit a certain level, you can exchange one low level card for one that’s a bit more powerful. There are 4 levels of cards.
2) Barbarian tokens on the board move at regular periods and they can end up destroying one of your caravans or claiming territory from you (which affects how much money your cities earn and how much you can advance)
3) Caravans allow you to gain trade tokens that can be used to increase the impact of your cards. For example, if you have two trade tokens on your military card, you can spend one or both to add a bonus to your roll. Caravans can also garner you another player’s Diplomacy card, which has certain benefits dependent on the card.
4) Placing a control tokens mean you’ve claimed territory (that particular space), which is necessary for collecting trade tokens (a “mature” city garners you a set number of trade tokens once you’ve “controlled” all adjacent tiles), collecting resources such as marble or diamonds, or for building cities (your build cities a certain number of spaces from a space you’ve controlled with a token).
5) The terrain has an impact on your choices. In order of scaled “easiness”, the terrains are 1-grasslands, 2-hills, 3-forest, 4-desert, and 5-mountains. To travel through a desert is considered difficult, so that 4 means your Economy card (the one that moves your caravan) needs to be in the 4 or 5 slot. Similary, to build a city in a mountain space means your Industry card has to be in the 5 slot.

There are more rules and factors that come into play, but that’s the general gist. As noted at the start, I’d say the learning curve is relatively steep the first time ( a lot of going back to the instruction booklet), but past the first game or two, it comes pretty easily. I’ve certainly played games with a far steeper curve and one that takes longer to get to know game play well. If I were ranking learning curves on a ten-point scale, I’d probably put this around a 6.

Turns move slowly the first time or two as people try to remember what they can do, what they need to do, etc. But after the first hour each player moves pretty quickly through their turns as you’ve gotten used to how to deal with the complexities of those shifting slots under the Focus bar. As people get closer to each other, things slow again as players try and figure out cost-benefit of attacking, but then as before, after a few attacks those move quickly.

I liked the game quite a bit. More than my two family members, but I tend to have more patience for the slowness of things and I mind long game less than they do. They did like it enough to play again. And as mentioned, I like that you can self-adjust your length simply by cutting out one of the agendas. It’s a game we’ll definitely keep and keep playing.

LiangCuber Tornado V3 M Flagship Speed Cube QY Toys X Man Tornado V3 Magnetic 3x3 Cube (Tornado V3 M Magnetic Core Flagship) When I got this, I still didn't solve the Rubik's cube. I know there are all kinds of tutorials, but I wanted to solve it on my own. Fast-forward 11 years later, I flipped the table (so to speak) and watched a couple tutorials. This was the cube I used to solve the puzzle for the first time. I watched a couple videos of the cube before receiving mine to get a better understanding of the mechanisms and design. During my first session, I set the magnets to the strongest and left the dials as they were. Two hours is how long it took me to solve it on the first try.

I like that this cube comes with a handful of accessories. I use the case to carry the cube with me to and from work. It stays on my desk; whenever I have to read something on my monitors and not use the keyboard, I solve a little bit. Now I can solve the cube in minutes, though it took me a few days to get to this point. I now have the spring and tension set to the strongest for how much force can be pulled and weakest for how fast turns can be. (Apologies for not using the correct terms, but I tried looking up what the dials exactly do and I still can't figure out which does what with regard to the terminology, but I base it off feel.)

The cube comes with a leather bag and a tool to adjust the magnets. The first time I accessed the dials, I used a pen to pop off the tiles. They can be difficult to pull off by hand alone, even after being pulled so many times. The lever for each dial also was difficult to pull. Now, I leave it semi-flush to the dial to make it easier to access in the future. They also pop off easily, but are [somewhat] easy to put back. The magnet levels sometimes move on their own. If I happen to notice a magnet at a strength I didn't set it at, I'll re-adjust. Annoying, but an easy fix. I no longer use the tool that came with the cube because any item small and flat enough will work. The bag is kept in the box for now.

There are two manuals that come with the cube: one for the cube itself and the other on how to solve it. I tried using the solve tutorial but found it confusing with some typographical errors, so I used videos. I learn better visually anyway. Even though the cube's manual has great illustrations for the mechanics, I failed to understand what they actually do, so I looked up videos for that too.

This is the third cube I own and currently it's my favorite. Each time my time lowers after solving, I adjust the settings. I'm becoming a speedcuber without realizing it.
text_fidelity_b: LiangCuber Tornado V3 M Flagship Speed Cube QY Toys X Man Tornado V3 Magnetic 3x3 Cube (Tornado V3 M Magnetic Core Flagship)

Terra by Battat – Wild Life Set – Realistic Animal Toy Figures with Elephant Toys for Kids 3+ (6 Pc) I have mixed feelings about this animal hospital. Overall, the structure itself is extremely sturdy and there are a lot of wonderful ideas in the construction. The roof swings up and down with a hinge, and while it's heavy enough that I have some cringes about someone getting a finger stuck, overall that concern has not panned out. The overall structure is very sturdy, but then the little animal pens have extremely flimsy doors, one of which didn't work right out the gate, and refuses to close. A second door also occasionally refuses to close, which makes me think that this is a design issue rather than a actual broken product. The really cool little deck that has a string fence is really a neat idea, but then it was implemented in such a flimsy fashion that it is really not that fun to play with because it keeps coming apart.

Overall I want to like this more, but when I compare it to something by Schleich which just has all of the details really dialed in to where nothing breaks or comes apart all the time, it's clear that there is a difference in quality. This is made nicely in some ways, but then falls short on some of those finished details.

I will also note that it took me a lot longer to assemble than I wish. I really think that they should have assembled some more parts of it and shipped it as a partly assembled things so that I didn't have to spend so much time putting it together. I have small children I would rather be hanging out with.

Pandemic on the Brink Board Game EXPANSION | Family /Strategy /Cooperative Board Game | Ages 8+ |2 to 5 players | Average Playtime 45 minutes | Made by Z-Man Games , Red Pandemic has become a favorite on game nights in my circle of friends, and the On the Brink Expansion improves the experience in several ways. There are new game modes, new roles, new events, and all of them work well. On the most basic level, the ability to have five players is a big improvement. You have to relearn the board setup some to compensate for how many new events are included to keep from unbalancing the game, but none of the changes are so drastic as to be overwhelming.

Aside from this, most of the new material boils down to making the game more difficult. The most basic form of this is the addition of an additional Epidemic card to enable "Legendary" difficulty (I think we lost in ten minutes the first time we tried that mode). The Virulent Strain variation to the rules increases the power of one of the diseases. The Mutation variation adds a fifth disease. All of these are good for the increased challenge, but don't really change the core gameplay too much.

The one exceptionally different mode is the Bio-Terrorist variation, which makes one player an enemy to the rest of the group. I, like many of the other reviewers, love this mode. My friends and roommates don't all agree. It is the type of game mode that certainly has the potential to ruin friendships if you play it too often, but I think it injects some welcome variety into the game. That said, it's totally optional and the expansion has plenty of other improvements to justify buying it even if this game mode doesn't prove to be a hit with your crowd.

As a last, wonderful feature, the game box comes packaged with a tray that is capable of holding the materials not only for the expansion, but for the original game as well. This way you can actually store the original game and the expansion in a single box. It sounds like a small thing, but little touches and details like that are what separate the good game publishers from the great.
text_fidelity_b: Pandemic on the Brink Board Game EXPANSION | Family /Strategy /Cooperative Board Game | Ages 8+ |2 to 5 players | Average Playtime 45 minutes | Made by Z-Man Games , Red

text_fidelity_a:
Melissa & Doug Created by Me! Owl Pillow, 6+ years Here are some observations from my wife.

My almost-5-year-old daughter LOVES this owl pillow craft project, and so do I! She and I have just begun working on sewing with a needle and thread, but I must be sure to be with her every minute, with my hands along with hers on our first sewing projects. This pillow, however, is so smartly designed that it allows her the freedom to practice sewing buttons ON HER OWN, and she loves that freedom. I can be close to her, at the sink, putting away dishes, while she creates her pillow all by herself. It’s a big deal to her. : )

I definitely had to sit with her at the start to go through the simple instructions and to get her started on the process. She enjoyed choosing her own pattern for the owl and decided to choose the same pattern as the owl of the adorable girl on the box. I showed her how to do the first few stitches, and then she was off and running. Once she got going on her own, she kept saying, “This is so easy! This is so fun!” while working on stitching through the felt buttons.

After our first hour on the project today, she’s definitely getting the hang of the process, and she can work on it on her own with me close by for the occasional help with knotting off a thread. And though she really wanted to be able to sleep with the pillow tonight, she’s excited to spend more time stitching the felt buttons onto her owl over the coming days. I’m glad that the project will take 5-7 days of stitching for her to complete. It’s longer than just an hour or even one-day project for her, since she’s at the young side of the recommended age range (6-10 years old). It’s possible an older child could finish this project in a few hours of an afternoon.

And I have to say that I’m thrilled that it’s machine washable. Overall, this is a fantastic and adorable craft for a little one at the very beginning stages of learning to sew.
text_fidelity_b: Melissa & Doug Created by Me! Owl Pillow, 6+ years

BOMENNE Build-on Brick Mug,Funny Novelty Coffee Mug Compatible with Lego,Creative DIY Building Blocks Cup,Birthday Party Cups For Kids,Unique Gifts For Christmas,Black I should have read some of the reviews before wasting money on these mugs.

I have spent the last 90 minutes trying to decorate this mug. The parts sent with the mug do not attach; you can place them but they immediately fall off. Those parts fit to one another very well, but they decline to play nicely (or at all) with their mug.

I tried LEGO pieces and they do not want to be pressed onto the mug. I really cannot blame them.

The only block pieces that do fit onto the mug are ones I had purchased from Dollar Tree. They meld easily with the mug and hold beautifully. Unfortunately, the only surface that will accept them is the front of the mug. As you can see from the pictures they are holding well, but the rest of the mug surfaces are...well, I am trying so hard not to be all negative and everything, but the mug is so poorly designed and sloppily made that nohting will attach at all, not LEGO, not the mug company's blocks and not even the pieces of white bread that I smushed together and tried to mold to the pegs and holes. It stuck whilst still moist and them fell off when it dried and I picked up the mug to check.

We are a totally dedicated LEGO family. We have even indoctrinated...coerced...um...lovingly brought my son-in-law into the LEGO Love. We give and share those precious bricks at every gifting opportunity. There have been times when my grandchildren are out playing with their friends and my daughter and I are still inside playing. I recently learned that the one set she would love to have is the Friend's Heartlake Hotel, but by that time it was already hovering around $400.00. I am thinking that I will make provisions in my will for her to have one.

Sadly, I bought two of these. Double the heartbreak. Do not buy this unless you are planning to do what I intend to do with them. I have a tiny ton of old costume jewelry that I use for crafting and I am going to use Gorilla Glue to cover the mug with some cool bits and bobs of jewelry. That will be a totally huge and groovy improvement to the really quite pathetic red C that is now on the mug. I am an old granny and am surprised how disappointed I am with this mug.

Please protect your loved ones and buy something else. You can buy some nice real LEGO packs for the $26.00 I wasted on this crap, or a very large amount of blocks and accessories of the blocks sold at Dollar Tree. Tell them I sent you.

Love,
Granny

text_fidelity_a:
Paw Patrol Mission Chase Figure (Due to the malfunctions on our particular dog, and the fact that he doesn't walk at all, I was tempted to give it 3 stars, but he's so cute and fun, I went with 4.)

I have a few Paw Patrol fans in my house, so this is a pretty amazing toy.

By pressing the badge on the front of Chase, your children are given a mission. Chase talks and interacts through these missions. For example, chickens have gotten loose, and your child needs to help gather them up. The net compartment opens up, and your child will fire the net out. Chase comments on catching one, and then asks for the net to be reloaded. (One time the net got stuck, and didn't fire out, but he still exclaimed praise at catching a chicken, so it's not perfect.) He won't interact to various things that your child says, but he does have built in interaction, which is still pretty cool.

There are 24 different missions, and Chase moves around a bit through these. I was expecting him to walk a bit, but he never did. He just moves his head around, and moves from crouching to standing positions. There are two compartments on his backpack. One has a net launcher. The other has a microphone(that your child can talk into) and a flashlight. There are various buttons for each feature. (One for opening each compartment, one on the net launcher to launch, one to make the light come on the flashlight, and one to turn on the microphone.) Some of the items come on automatically through missions, but others require your child's assistance, when Chase asks.

Although this is an awesome toy that I'm pretty sure any Paw Patrol fan will love, we did have a couple of negatives with ours.

When the box was first opened, the head was detached a bit, but thankfully, it went back on pretty easily. Also, the button to launch the microphone/flashlight wouldn't work. I tried everything I could to make it work, short of tearing it apart, and tried numerous times, but it never worked. It didn't work when it was supposed to automatically open during missions, either. Thankfully, we can just pull that compartment open. During missions when a child is asked to launch the microphone/flashlight, pulling open the door makes the task recognized, just as if the button worked. So, it's not a huge deal, but still disappointing.

I really do wish he walked a bit, too! The way he's designed, it looked as if he would.

A couple of notes:
-This toy DOES come with batteries, but require 4 AA if you'd like to buy extras.
-If your child can read, know that the box this is delivered in says what's inside, though there are no pictures.
text_fidelity_b: Paw Patrol Mission Chase Figure

text_fidelity_a:
CVCBSER Smooth Swing Dueling Lightsaber, Increase Motion Control 12 Sets Sound Effect Light Saber, with 16 Colors Changeable Premium Metal Handle Lightsabers for Adults and Boys Gift (Silver) [[VIDEOID:acf24d91cee31c0de845571b6cd24d7b]] This is a very nice light saber. Good heft to it with lots of features. There will be a learning curve, but hopefully my tips as well as the video demo will make it easier for you. Remember that it is all in the blinking:

After assembling and charging your saber, you start off in SLEEP mode, meaning NOTHING should be illuminated. Hold the power button until the power ring illuminates and you hear a voice saying POWER ON. Now this is called OFF/AWAKE mode. Off meaning the lights/effects are not turned on yet, but the power button ring is illuminated. More on this OFF/AWAKE state later. But here, you simply tap the button to turn on the lights and effects. Now you are in ON/AWAKE mode, and here are the commands for ON/AWAKE mode:

ON/AWAKE MODE COMMANDS:
-------------------------------------
ONE BLINK: Hold the button until it BLINKS one time, then release. LOCK-UP effect is now enabled. It basically sounds like your saber just hit some electrical wires and is going crazy. Tap the button to get out of it.

TWO BLINKS: Hold the button until it BLINKS twice, then release. The saber will cycle through the color choices. Once you like a color, tap to set your color choice.

THREE BLINKS: Hold the button until it BLINKS three times, then release. You will hear a quote from the movies. To hear a different quote, hold until it BLINKS three times again, then release. Basically keep holding and releasing after three blinks to cycle through the quotes.

FOUR BLINKS: This turns OFF the lights/effects. But, the power ring is still illuminated, which means you are back to OFF/AWAKE mode, and here are the commands for OFF/AWAKE mode:

OFF/AWAKE MODE COMMANDS:
--------------------------------------
ONE BLINK: This allows you to set the sound volume. You can set between NO SOUND, LOUD SOUND, and SOFT SOUND.

TWO BLINKS: This is for light effects. You can have it STABLE, UNSTABLE, or PULSE. Stable gives a consistent solid light, which is what I have on during my demo because it's easier to capture on video.

THREE BLINKS: This is for setting a theme music. You can cycle through 5 songs, and the 6th is no music. So if you leave it at any one of the songs, whenever to turn on the lights/effects, music will be on too. So if you don't want any music, make sure you cycle all the way to no music.

FOUR BLINKS: You can cycle through more movie quotes, one of which is, "The force is with you Luke..."

LASTLY, to put it sleep. Hold the button for 10 seconds, so when you do this. It will go through its blinking, but just disregard them until the red illumination is completely off. This takes about 10 seconds. You are now in SLEEP mode. The same mode as when you first assembled and charged the saber. To play again, hold the power button until it illuminates, and you are back to OFF/AWAKE mode.
text_fidelity_b: CVCBSER Smooth Swing Dueling Lightsaber, Increase Motion Control 12 Sets Sound Effect Light Saber, with 16 Colors Changeable Premium Metal Handle Lightsabers for Adults and Boys Gift (Silver)

text_fidelity_a:
Arizona GameCo Smack it! Card Game for Kids | Ages 6-12 | Fun, Fast-paced and Easy to Learn | Family Game Night Friendly | a Great Boy or Girl Gift Idea Fairly fun game but card quality is poor for the price. I doubt this is a game to play for hours on end yet.....at the price point I would appreciate brand playing card quality. Is the game bad? I have "dealt" with worse.....there are certainly other card games....even Uno; cheaper, with better card quality but after all....this is a fast slap game. The cards feel cheap, look cheap and shuffle the same. They shuffle in a manegable way but to me this is almost disposable card stock quality. The "art" is non existent with numbers simple written and spelled on the card...colors also do not matter.
Your kids might just toss them on the table and mish mosh them to shuffle them. That will work fine. Slamwich has the excellent card quality and is also a fast easy slap game along this price point. If I had a re-do, I would just stick with Slamwich. Card stock is higher quality and game itself is a little more in depth and kids and adults enjoy a few rounds.

I cannot in good conscience recommend this at 8 dollars or higher. The gameplay itself is simple old fashioned war with a light/slight twist. Number cards....say a 14 verus a 32 dont matter at all (the 32 doesnt take the pile)....it is all about the "slap cards" and "challenege cards"...challenge is where your higher number card played actually counts for once. I DO see that very young kids would enjoy it. I do not see this being a "drinking game" or fun for adults without some extra house rules. Quality is simply subpar for the price. The business is in the USA, the cards and actual game itself are outsourced to China if that matters to you.

Rating is ....average. These are close or are average card size....they have a slick coat. The plain white background quickly picks up color bleed or whatever.....

It is not horrible but just eeks in at "ok" for simple card games. It isnt great and it isnt a big go to except for maybe the 7 year old children set...and the box states...6 plus for age and 2 to 7 people. I say...skip don't smack.

I had to try this one out.

If you've never used an infinity cube before, they're the latest in fun fidgety-toy types of thing, but also kind of more interesting because they bend and fold in ways that feel like it is constantly turning into something else. Sort like a transformer toy that goes on forever.

I really like the wood color and style of this, but my first impression wasn't very good. It was a lot harder to move and the wooden blocks would get stuck on each other as you bend and fold. Not anywhere near as smooth as the plastic variants. But the cords that hold this together just need some stretching to loosen them up. Once you've broken it in, it moves much more smoothly and eventually will give you the satisfying feel that an infinity cube is known for. I can't speak for the longevity of it yet, I am a little concerned that in the same way you need to break this in, it can also eventually stretch out and/or snap. text_fidelity_a:
IDO3D Pen and Ink Up to 25 Projects Print System - 5 pens What a great creative art toy. You can do literally anything with this and takes your sketches off the paper and into three dimensions. I am amazed at the ways the kids put this into practice, and it kept them engrossed for hours with only a couple squabbles over people hogging this color or that. I'll get more into what we did below. But first, What you get and How this works.

This product is a hardening gel that can be squeezed into shapes using plastic forms. There are several forms that come with the kit, a flat sheet of plastic and a couple rounded forms for creating spherical shapes. The flat clear piece is great for tracing images so even young kids can achieve the shapes they desire. Also, we used it to make other curves to help flesh out animal shapes, but that proved a little more difficult.

Once you have drawn your shapes with one of the gel pens, you can use the UV flashlight to harden the pieces to make them retain the shapes you want. Then you can peel them off the plastic forms or sheet and cement elements together into three dimensional structures. The possibilities are endless and only limited by creativity. Our kids started out by tracing the provided dinosaurs and moved on to tracing other dinos from various books until they had a small forest of dinos and trees.

Warnings and caveats: I'm a little leery of the chemically nature of this toy. There are warnings to avoid skin contact in light. This put me a little on edge and I wanted to supervise our 8 through 14 year olds to make sure it was not getting on skin or other stuff. Also, this does take a bit of artistic ability. It can be as free form as you want it to be, but we did have some frustration when younger kids could not recreate the stuff the older kids were building. But for the most part it was very conducive to creativity.

Also, the end products are a little sticky. So they don't seem like you can play with your creations, but you can make wonderful visual art. We have a nice little dino diorama on our book shelf now and the kids seem pretty proud of it. The inks are also a little messy, so make sure your in a cleanable area.

Personally, I think this is one of the most wonderfully novel and creative ideas I've seen in a while. I will be picking up some for the kids on my Christmas list, and look forward to refilling our supply.
text_fidelity_b: IDO3D Pen and Ink Up to 25 Projects Print System - 5 pens

Hasbro Gaming Battleship Shots We've only had this a few days so far, but my kids love it so far! They and their neighborhood friends were playing almost non-stop this entire weekend. It's a pretty unique concept and not at all what I expected coming from the original battleship: Rather than the game of strategy (and sometimes just luck!) that the traditional battleship is, this is mostly a game of skill. There is still some strategy in how you align your boats, but rather than try to determine where the other player's position is, you can see their board and have to toss one of the included ping-pong balls into the holes. Land a ball in all the boat's places, and you've sunk their ship! It is definitely reminiscent of beer pong in skillset, or perhaps one of those arcade games that require you to land a ball in a colored cup. You definitely need more space to play since there will be balls bouncing around if/when you miss, but it is a lot of fun. A creative twist on a classic game!
One thing that is a little strange to me however, is the advertising. The listing for this product says "Nostalgic tabletop gameplay meets interactive digital content for an immersive gaming experience". There's nothing digital about this, let alone interactive digital and immersive. It's a pretty fun analog pick-up-and-play game, which is what I like about it actually, but it was hard to determine what we were getting before we tried it.
text_fidelity_b: Hasbro Gaming Battleship Shots

The gold tips on the blades are a nice touch, to match the other gold trim on the P3P. This type of blade also fits many other quadcopters that use the same type screw on propeller shaft, replacing the slip on props and lock nuts, which often come off during flight, causing a lot of crashes, damage and even lost quads. My advice is always use the self tightening props. But, avoid those with metal hubs. The metal hubs will either lock on too tight or not tight enough. Composite hubs, like these, are always best.

Friends TV Show Collage Jigsaw Puzzle 1000 Pieces Officially Licensed Friends TV Show Merchandise EDIT: initially I reviewed this before really getting into the puzzle. I’m in it now, and I can say this is one of the most poorly formulated puzzles I’ve ever done. It appears that whoever decided the pattern of the piece cut outs was lazy and decided to have repeating shapes throughout, which results in many perfect fits that are completely incorrect. In places where the differences are obvious, it’s not much of an issue, but there are also plenty of times this happens in areas that look similar, resulting in incorrect placement, backtracking, and frustration. I love puzzles, but not this one. I love friends, but I can’t stand this friends puzzle. The visual design was excellent, so whoever came up with that did a wonderful job. Lots of nostalgia, lots of little visual cues to make it fun. But whoever designed the cut out portion did an awful job.

So the puzzle itself isn’t super high res, nor are the pieces particularly inventive in how they’re cut, but man am I having fun reliving the show. Honestly, this is all about the nostalgia and having a chill time. It’s a little harder than I expected, but still totally doable. Perfect escape!
text_fidelity_b: Friends TV Show Collage Jigsaw Puzzle 1000 Pieces Officially Licensed Friends TV Show Merchandise

text_fidelity_a:
SYMA X22W Mini Drone with Camera Live Video FPV Pocket Drone for Kids and Beginners, RC Quadcopter with App Control, Altitude Hold, 3D Flips, Headless Mode and Bonus Battery, Red I always wanted to have a small drone to be able to inspect parts of my house inaccessible to me like my roof and the gutters. I was surprised how small the drone was when I received it. It fit in the palm of my hand. After reading through the directions twice, I thought I had a basic idea on how to operate the drone. I downloaded the app, connected to it via WiFi and had the propellers spinning up and that’s when things kinda lost control. The drone flew up a few feet but also flew forward (or backwards) even though I wasn’t touching the right control stick which is supposed to do that. Up and down seemed to be working fine, but with the drone constantly flying sideways, it was impossible to control properly. Even when using the right control stick, it seemed to only acknowledge forwards, and wouldn’t respond to the other direction. Then the drone suddenly dropped the WiFi connection within 10 minutes. Powering off and on didn’t fix it. I took the battery out, put it back in and was connected again for a minute or two before the battery just died completely. Yes, I fully charged the battery before use. Surely this products battery should last more than 15 minutes of intermittent usage.
Overall, as someone familiar with remote control devices and technology, I found this drone difficult to control and hence no fun to use.
text_fidelity_b: SYMA X22W Mini Drone with Camera Live Video FPV Pocket Drone for Kids and Beginners, RC Quadcopter with App Control, Altitude Hold, 3D Flips, Headless Mode and Bonus Battery, Red

He fits on this perfectly but even after he outgrows it, he will still love it- Half the time he prefers to push it around rather than ride it!

The recording for the music is definitely grainy, as many other reviewers have noted. I don't mind this and neither does my son but if that will be a deal-breaker for you, it's better that you know now. If you squeeze one ear, the horse sings and the mouth moves. If you squeeze the other ear, a random saying will come out. My son loves pressing the ears and then hurries to kneel down and watch the horse's mouth move. He loves hugging this little guy and when he prefers to rock on it, he will bring me the base so I can put it back on- which takes a whole 2 seconds; you just set it down on top of the rocker base, pull the plastic piece over the front bar and close until it clicks. Voila! To make it a rideable toy again, you simply push the button and the plastic piece pops open to release the horse.

I definitely recommend this little horse for 1 year olds and up. At almost 2 years old, my son has a while to go before he won't fit on this anymore. This was definitely a good buy and worth every penny!
